issues.failure_explanation: The abstract asserts that the hyperbolic-cost policy 'on average outperforms MTD and AT in terms of time to progression'. The paper's own Table 3 contradicts this for n_0=0.25, where the hyperbolic policy's mean is 102 days versus 210 (MTD) and 213 ('On-Off' AT), i.e., less than half. Moreover, the quantity reported for this policy is not the TTP of eq:def_TTP but the modified $\tau_{TTP'}$ (last instant at or below the progression threshold), and under this policy the tumor crosses the progression threshold during the initial treatment-free phase, so even in the favorable settings the outperformance holds only for the redefined metric while being announced as 'time to progression'.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mu_N\coloneqq \delta_{1.5}  \otimes \delta_0 \otimes\frac{1}{25}\sum_{j=1}^{25} \delta_{\hat r_R^j} \otimes \frac{1}{49}\sum_{k=1}^{49} \delta_{\hat f_0^k},
\Theta_N \coloneqq \{1.5\} \times \{0\} \times \{0.5,0.52,\ldots,1\} \times \{0.002,0.004, \ldots, 0.1\},
we discretized the interval $[0.5,1]$ where $\hat r_R$ varies into $25$ equi\-spaced nodes with distance $0.02$
we divided the interval $[0.002,1]$ into $49$ nodes with a constant step equal to $0.002$
The mean TTP is computed by taking the average over the elements of the set $\Theta_N$ (see \cref{eq:Theta_N_simul}).

issues.failure_explanation: The grid specifications are mutually inconsistent. The set {0.5,0.52,...,1} contains (1-0.5)/0.02+1 = 26 points, not 25, and {0.002,0.004,...,0.1} contains (0.1-0.002)/0.002+1 = 50 points, not 49; hence $\Theta_N$ as defined in eq:Theta_N_simul has 26*50 = 1300 elements, contradicting the claimed support size N = 1225 = 25*49 and the weights 1/25 and 1/49 in $\mu_N$. In addition, 25 equispaced nodes at distance 0.02 cannot cover [0.5,1], and 'dividing [0.002,1] into 49 nodes with step 0.002' is wrong on both the interval and the count. As written, the discrete ensemble actually simulated (which 25 of the 26 $\hat r_R$-nodes and which 49 of the 50 $\hat f_0$-nodes are used, or whether all nodes were used with weights 1/26 and 1/50) cannot be determined, and $\mu_N$ as written is not supported on all of $\Theta_N$.

failure_location.quote: which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the grid specification consistent (e.g., 26 and 50 equispaced nodes with weights 1/26 and 1/50 and N=1300, or explicitly listed 25- and 49-node grids matching the weights), and align the table captions that average over $\Theta_N$.
issues.overall_effect: The ensemble underlying every simulation and every mean/max/min TTP reported in Tables 1, 3, and 4 is not reproducible as specified, and the cardinality claim N=1225 is false with respect to eq:Theta_N_simul. No theoretical result depends on the grid.
issues.title: Internally inconsistent discretization of the parameter ensemble (25/49 nodes vs node sets of 26/50 points; N=1225 vs 1300)

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}^\theta \coloneqq \inf_{\tau>0}\{ s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau) \geq 1.2\, n_0 \}
\tau_{\mathrm{TTP'}}^\theta \coloneqq \sup_{\tau>0}\{ s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau) \leq 1.2\, n_0 \}

issues.failure_explanation: Uniqueness of the instant at which the population equals 1.2n_0 does not imply $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}} = \tau_{\mathrm{TTP}'}$. If the trajectory touches the level 1.2n_0 tangentially at $\bar\tau$ (population at least 1.2n_0 only at the single instant $\bar\tau$, strictly below before and after, which is realizable in this model, e.g., when free growth peaks exactly at the threshold and subsequent treatment drives the tumor down), then {tau : s+r >= 1.2n_0} = {$\bar\tau$}, so $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}=\bar\tau$, while {tau : s+r <= 1.2n_0} = (0,infty), so $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}'}=+\infty \neq \bar\tau$. The claimed equality requires an additional hypothesis (e.g., that the trajectory stays above 1.2n_0 after $\bar\tau$), which is missing; notably, threshold-touching trajectories are exactly what the later 'Off-On' policy produces.

failure_location.quote: If for some $\theta$ there exists a unique instant $\bar \tau >0$ such that $s^\theta(\bar \tau) + r^\theta(\bar \tau) = 1.2\, n_0$, then it turns out that $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}^\theta  = \tau_{\mathrm{TTP'}}^\theta = \bar \tau$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis to the remark (the trajectory remains above 1.2n_0 after the instant, i.e., the level is properly crossed), or state the equality only under that condition.
issues.overall_effect: The remark's justification for equating TTP and TTP' is unsound in the tangential-touch case. No labelled result depends on it, but it underpins the paper's informal substitution of TTP' for TTP.
issues.title: Remark's criterion for equality of TTP and TTP' fails under tangential touching of the progression threshold
issues.why_classification: A one-line local strengthening of the hypothesis repairs the assertion; nothing downstream relies on the defective version.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: At $\tau =0$, set {$u=0$} and keep it constant while $s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau)<  1.2\, n_0$ (vacation period).
After observing $s^\theta(\tau)+r^\theta(\tau)\geq 1.2\, n_0$, reset {$u=1$} and keep it constant while  $s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau)> n_0/2$ (treatment period).
\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}^\theta \coloneqq \inf_{\tau>0}\{ s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau) \geq 1.2\, n_0 \}
We insist on the fact that for having a fair evaluation of the TTP, in the rows marked as `Hyperbolic' (corresponding to the cost $\ell^2$), we used $\tau_{TTP'}^\theta$.
Hyperbolic &$0.25$ &  $672$ days & $9$ days & $102$ days\
The TTP of `On-Off'~AT and `Off-On'~AT is $424$ days and $459$ days, respectively, with a progression delay of $5$ weeks.
The outcomes of `Off-On'~AT seem promising, as it shows an improvement in almost every performance indicator compared to `Off-On'~AT.

issues.failure_explanation: By construction, the 'Off-On' policy keeps u=0 until the total population reaches 1.2n_0, which is exactly the progression threshold used in the definition of TTP (eq:def_TTP). During a vacation with $\hat d_T=0$ the population grows monotonically toward the carrying capacity 1 (since $\dot n = (1-n)(s+\hat r_R r) > 0$), so it attains $s+r \geq 1.2n_0$ within the short initial free-growth phase (roughly 9-10 days for n_0=0.25 and about 40 days for n_0=0.75; the 9-day worst-case TTP' for the hyperbolic policy in Table 3 confirms this free-growth timescale). Hence for every theta the defined $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}$ under 'Off-On' AT is this small initial-growth time: the disease is 'in progression' from the end of the first vacation onward. The values reported in Table 4 (107-1500 days) and in the Fig. Off-On caption (459 days) therefore cannot be $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}$; they are consistent only with $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}'}$ (the instant of definitive escape above the threshold), a metric substitution the paper discloses only for the 'Hyperbolic' rows of Table 3 and never for Table 4. Consequently the caption's claim that Table 4 is a TTP comparison, and the claim that 'Off-On' AT improves on 'On-Off' AT, are unsupported under the paper's own definition of progression: under TTP, 'Off-On' AT progresses within weeks, far earlier than every strategy in Table 1. (The max value of 1500 days for n_0=0.75 also coincides with the horizon $T_{\mathrm{hor}}$, indicating possible undisclosed censoring.)

failure_location.quote: Comparison in terms of Time-to-Progression (TTP) between `On-Off'~AT and `Off-On'~AT.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Relabel the 'Off-On' AT entries of Table 4 and the Fig. Off-On caption as $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}'}$ (time of definitive escape above the progression threshold), state explicitly that by construction the policy brings the tumor to the threshold 1.2n_0 at the end of every vacation (so TTP equals the initial free-growth time), and correspondingly weaken the TTP-improvement claims in the caption, Section 3.4, abstract, and introduction; alternatively, set the vacation switching threshold strictly below 1.2n_0 and rerun the experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The reported performance and comparative claims for the proposed 'Off-On' AT (Table 4, the Fig. Off-On caption, the improvement statement in Section 3.4, and the abstract/introduction 'promising results' claims) are unreliable as statements about time to progression; they are meaningful only after relabeling them as TTP'-type quantities (time to definitive loss of control).
issues.title: 'Off-On' AT results are reported as TTP but cannot be TTP under the paper's own definitions
issues.why_classification: A supported repair (relabeling the metric and qualifying the claims) preserves all reported numbers and the qualitative conclusion in the TTP' sense, but it necessarily changes the meaning of a headline performance claim from 'time to progression' to 'time to definitive escape', and the alternative repair requires redoing the simulations.
